snip.t: The RBC life span is much shorter in patients with hemolysis secondary to conditions such as hereditary spherocytosis, immune hemolytic anemia, or sickle cell disease.\n
Hereditary spherocytosis (HS) is a common cause of inherited hemolytic anemia, with a prevalence of approximately 1 in 2,000-5,000 persons.\n
Hereditary spherocytosis is usually transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.\n
Hereditary spherocytosis is the most common inherited hemolytic anemia in persons of northern European descent.
RBC membrane: Defects (e.g., hereditary spherocytosis) make cells fragile → splenic sequestration
Membrane disorders: Hereditary spherocytosis, hereditary elliptocytosis
Underlying haematological disorders – sickle cell disease (auto‑antibodies, functional asplenia), thalassaemia, hereditary spherocytosis.
Osmotic fragility(rbcs resistance to hemolysis-thalassemia /hereditary spherocytosis)

qs.q: Most common cause of hereditary spherocytosis?
qs.e: Ankyrin defects (isolated or combined with spectrin) are the most frequent cause.

qs.q: Hereditary spherocytosis is most commonly due to deficiency of
qs.e: Spectrin/ankyrin deficiency destabilizes the RBC membrane skeleton, causing membrane loss and spherocyte formation with reduced osmotic resistance.
